READ_THIS_BEFORE_THE_MISMATCHES: A MISMATCH IN THIS FILE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A BUILD PROBLEM. The replay uses run_go2_finetune_verdict.arm_cmd, which reproduces only the flag set the verdict harness needs. Where it cannot reproduce a dataset's original invocation, the replay differs for reasons that have nothing to do with Chrono. Proven insufficient three independent ways, below. 6 datasets are VERIFIED; the other 13 are UNDETERMINED BY THIS INSTRUMENT; zero show any sign of a build problem.

why_the_instrument_is_insufficient.1_terrain_is_hardcoded: arm_cmd passes --terrain rigid unconditionally. go2_stratified and go2_merged are CRM datasets, so the replay ran different physics and produced no comparable CSV at all.
why_the_instrument_is_insufficient.2_no_torque_perturbation_flag: arm_cmd passes --perturb-peak-n (force) and has no torque equivalent. go2_torque_fwd's episodes carry perturbation torque up to 33.1 Nm with perturbation force identically zero, so the replay could not reproduce them. Applies to the torque and pairprobe datasets.
why_the_instrument_is_insufficient.3_the_spec_does_not_determine_the_output: go2_stand_tilt, go2_standpose_0 and go2_tilt_walkable yield IDENTICAL replay specs (off=5000000, seed=2000, roll=-1.75, pitch=2.80, prewalk=1.08) but contain different data. At most one could have matched. The episode sidecar therefore omits something that determines the output, which makes a mismatch uninformative about anything else.

also_unrecorded_the_checkpoint: No sidecar records which policy checkpoint produced the episode, so even a well-formed replay confounds build with policy. A MATCH rules out both at once and is the only clean verdict available; a mismatch separates neither.
